newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Austria's new chancellor backs EU jobs push.
newsitem.headline: Austria's new chancellor backs EU jobs push.

text.p: Austrian Chancellor Viktor Klima on Thursday pledged Austria's full support for efforts by the Dutch European Union presidency to boost employment across the 15-member bloc.

"We need joint initiatives, joint measures to increase employment," Klima said, adding that job creation need not depend on Brussels launching new projects which would involve fresh contributions from member states.
Austria is grappling with high unemployment which soared above 300,000 in January, its highest level since 1956.
Klima, on his first official foreign visit since becoming chancellor in January, was talking to journalists at a joint news conference with Wim Kok after a meeting with the Dutch prime minister.

Asked whether the Dutch EU presidency supported Austria's continued neutrality as a European member state, Kok said that European member states were free to make up their own minds whether or not to join NATO.
"This is an issue of sovereignty," Kok said.
Klima's social democrats, backed by a clear majority of Austrians, have resisted tampering with the nation's neutral status, which is enshrined in Austria's post-World War Two constitution.
Kok told reporters that the two leaders had also discussed environmental issues and the fight against illegal drugs as well as Intergovernmental Conference (IGC) issues.
As current holder of the revolving EU presidency the Netherlands is due to set the seal on a new European treaty by concluding the IGC at an Amsterdam summit in June.
